place.zh: 外门演武场 · 五行台
place.en: The outer court training ground · the Five Elements Platform

setup.zh: 你站在台心，把那只手翻过来，低头看着自己的掌心。
setup.en: You stand at the centre of the platform, turn that hand over, and look down at your palm.

recap.zh: 你的掌心烙下一个印子：一个圈，圈里一横，搓不掉。决赛，祁长松站在台心「我不碰你」；你脑门上贴着猪蜻蜓，日落风一掉头，一头扎向他，他让了一步，你脸朝下拍在台心，香到，赢了。观主把筑基丹放在你左手里；褚先生搭了你的右腕：「脉上是二层。……掌上不是。」
recap.en: A mark was branded in your palm: a circle with a bar across it, and it won't rub off. In the final Qi Changsong stood at the centre — "I won't touch you"; with the pig-copter on your forehead you rode the turning sunset wind and dived at him, he stepped aside, you landed face down on the centre, the incense ran out, and you won. The abbot put the Foundation pill in your left hand; Master Chu took your right wrist: "By the pulse, layer two. …By the palm, not."

zh: 掌心正中，烙着一个印子。
en: In the middle of the palm, a brand.
A circle, with a bar across it.

story.zh:
小满站在台心，把那只手翻过来，低头看着自己的掌心。

掌心正中，烙着一个印子。不红，不肿，是一道一道发白的细线，像是从肉里头长出来的：一个圈，圈里一横。

他拿拇指去搓，搓不掉；拿指甲去刮，刮得皮都红了，那个圈，那一横，还在那里，白白的，凉凉的。

胸口的木牌凉了下来，一个很低的声音在他耳朵里道：「……你拿手接了。」小满小声道：「嗯。」那声音隔了很久，才又道：「……傻子。」便没有声息了。

台上台下两百来人，一个声音也没有。褚先生站在人群最后头，一只手捋着山羊胡子，捋到一半，停在半空。隔了好一会儿，才有一个声音怯生生地道：「……他……他那是……反噬了吧？」这一声给众人打开了一扇门：「对对对，反噬！吃丹吃坏了！」「一夜吞了三瓶丹，灵力是虚的！」「褚先生讲过的，轻则退三层，重则废！」「我就说他脸上那些斑不对劲！」越说越信，越信越觉得自己早就看出来了。褚先生的山羊胡子终于落了下来，他咳了一声，沉着脸道：「丹药之道，贪多必失。诸位引以为戒。」说罢转身走了，走的时候，回头看了小满一眼，看的是他垂在身边的那只手。

当时没有人问沈小满练气几层。只有两个人不这么觉得。一个是台北面竹椅上的观主玄沉子，他从头到尾没动过，这时候却轻轻「嗯」了一声。另一个是山门台阶上的瞿老，他背对着演武场，一直在扫地；镜子裂开的那一声，他的扫帚停了，停在那一级台阶上。那一级台阶，他扫了五十年，这一天，没有扫完。
story.en:
Xiaoman stood at the centre of the stage, turned his hand over, and looked down at his palm.

In the middle of the palm a mark was branded. Not red, not swollen: fine white lines, as if they had grown out of the flesh — a circle, with a bar across it.

He rubbed it with his thumb and it didn't rub off; he scraped it with a nail till the skin went red, and the circle, the bar, were still there, white, cold.

The token on his chest cooled, and a very low voice said in his ear: "…You caught it with your hand." "Mm," he whispered. A long while later the voice said: "…Fool." And then nothing.

Two hundred-odd people on and off the stage, and not a sound. At the very back, Master Chu stood with a hand on his goatee, stopped halfway down. After a long while a timid voice said: "…He… that was… backlash, wasn't it?" That opened a door: "Yes, yes, backlash! Ate too many pills!" "Three bottles in one night — his power's hollow!" "Master Chu told us — at best you drop three layers, at worst you're crippled!" "I knew those blotches weren't right!" The more they said it the more they believed it, and the more they believed it the surer they were they'd seen it all along. Master Chu's goatee finally came down. He coughed, and said sternly: "In the way of pills, greed brings loss. Take warning, all of you." He turned to go, and going, looked back once at Xiaoman — at the hand hanging at his side.

At the time, nobody asked Shen Xiaoman what layer he was. Only two people thought otherwise. One was the abbot Xuanchenzi in the bamboo chair north of the stage; he hadn't moved the whole time, but now he gave a soft "Mm." The other was Old Qu on the gate steps, his back to the training ground, sweeping all along; at the sound of the mirror cracking his broom stopped, stopped on that one step. That step he had swept for fifty years; that day, he never finished it.

label.zh: 攥着拳上台：决赛，对祁长松
label.en: Up with your fist hidden: the final, against Qi Changsong

exits.means: the final against Qi Changsong, who will not touch him: the pig-copter on his forehead at the turn of the sunset wind, the dive at the man who stands like a tree, the one step aside, the gong — then the jade box taken left-handed, the branded right hand hidden

story.zh:
日头挨着西边山尖的时候，另一个半边也打完了。祁长松在台心站了半炷香，内门那个七层把一套掌法打了三遍，打得满头大汗，香一灭，执事一看，台心上站着的还是他。

决赛，沈小满对祁长松。

小满上台的时候，右手攥着拳，藏在袖子里。祁长松已经站在了台心，两只脚钉在那道拼缝上，袍角都不动。他看了一眼小满的袖子，道：「马师弟那一镜，你接了。」小满道：「他自己照干了。」祁长松道：「我不碰你。」说完，眼皮一垂，再不说话。香点着了。

小满绕着他走了一圈，又走了一圈。他上去推，推他的胳膊，像推一根柱子；他抱住祁长松的腰往外扳，扳得脸都红了，祁长松低头看看他，像看一只扒在树干上的猴子。小满松了手，退到台边喘气。香，烧下去一半了。台下有人喊：「二层的，下来吧，别耽误人家吃晚饭！」

小满从怀里摸出那个本子，从本子里抽出一张黄纸来。台下的人伸长了脖子：一只猪，背上两对翅膀。「符？」「二层的人画的符？」「画的是猪？」小满舔了舔那张纸的背面，往自己脑门上一拍。

没有风。他站在台边，脑门上贴着一只猪，等着。台下的笑声一浪高过一浪，钱掌柜在老槐树底下把算盘都笑掉了。小满不笑。他爹说过，日头落山那一下，山里的风要掉个头——白天往山上走，夜里往山下走；掉头的那一下，林子里的鹿都要抬头。先看风，后看鹿。

日头沉下去了。演武场边上那面旗先是一垂，跟着「哗」地翻了个面。胸口的木牌极轻地暖了一暖，像有人在被窝里翻了个身，吹了一口气。小满两只脚离了地。

他飘起来，飘得并不好看：头朝前，屁股朝后，两条腿在半空里乱蹬，先撞上演武场东角那棵老柏，「咚」的一声，弹回来；又撞上西角那棵，「咚」的一声，又弹回来。台下的人抱着脑袋四下乱躲，一个内门师兄的发髻给他一脚踢歪了。他在半空里打了个转，脑门上那只猪冲着台心，不动了——台心上站着一个人，两只脚钉在石头里，二十年没挪过一步，站得比哪棵树都像树。

猪蜻蜓认树。

它一头扎了下来，小满跟着它，头朝下，嘴里「哇——」的一声，直奔祁长松的面门。

祁长松站了二十年。可一个人脑门上贴着一只猪，哇哇叫着，头朝下往他脸上扎，这样的事，二十年里没有过。他眉头一皱，往旁边让了一步——只一步，让得极轻巧，袍角都没乱。

小满扎在了台心上，脸朝下，正正地拍在五块青石板拼缝的那一点上，四肢摊开，像一张贴在门板上的年画。脑门上那张黄纸，「嘶」地撕成了两半。

便在这时，执事敲响了铜锣。那半炷香，到了。

执事看看台心上趴着的那一个，又看看台心外头一步站着的那一个，张了两回嘴，才道：「……沈小满，胜。」

演武场上静了好一会儿。祁长松低头看着自己挪开的那只脚，看了很久，道：「二十年。」又道：「你那张符，哪来的？」小满从地上爬起来，捂着鼻子：「……捡的。」祁长松看着他，没说信，也没说不信，冲他点了一点头，走下了台。

冠军，筑基丹一枚。照观里的老例，冠军的名字要写进那本蓝布面的名录。周衡把名录摊开，往前翻了几十页，翻到划了一道的那一页，看了一眼，才又翻回来——三十年，这一行头一回要写外门的名字。人群后头一阵骚动，马小宝回来了，裹着他爹的棉袍，头发上结着冰碴子，湿淋淋地一路走，一路滴水，滴到五行台跟前，看见观主正把一只玉盒子往沈小满手里放，站住了，张了张嘴，什么也没说出来，打了一个寒战。他手里还攥着那面裂了的镜子，落水的时候也没撒手。他看看裂镜，又看看小满垂在身边、攥得紧紧的那只拳头，把裂镜揣进了怀里。

那玉盒子玉色青白，盒盖上贴着一道封条，封条上盖着观主的大印。小满把左手伸出去接，右手攥着拳，藏在袖子里。玄沉子把玉盒放在他手里，手却没有马上松开，温和地道：「沉鼎秘境里，有一间石室。三百年，没人进去过……」他没说完，拍了拍他的肩膀，转身走了。小满捧着玉盒站在那里，后背上的汗，一下子全冒了出来。

他捧着玉盒走下五行台的时候，往山门那边望了一眼。瞿老站在台阶上，拄着扫帚，也在看。可瞿老看的不是他，是他手里那只玉盒子。那一眼很长，长得不像是在看一只盒子，倒像是在看一件很多年以前的旧事。然后瞿老转过身去，扫地了。

台阶底下，褚先生在等他。人都往伙房那边散了，老先生一个人站在那里，冲他伸出两根指头：「腕子。」小满把左腕递过去。褚先生不接，道：「那一只。」小满站了一会儿，把右手从袖子里伸了出来。褚先生搭了很久，久到山门那边瞿老的扫帚又响了起来。他把那只手翻过来，看了一眼掌心，又翻了回去，松了手，道：「脉上是二层。」捋了一下山羊胡子，转身走了，走出去三步，头也不回，又补了一句：「掌上不是。」
story.en:
When the sun touched the western peaks, the other half was done too. Qi Changsong stood at the centre for half a stick; the inner-court layer seven went through a whole set of palm strikes three times over, till the sweat poured off him; the incense burned out, the steward looked, and the one at the centre was still him.

The final: Shen Xiaoman against Qi Changsong.

When Xiaoman went up, his right hand was a fist, hidden in his sleeve. Qi Changsong already stood at the centre, feet nailed to the seam, not a fold of his robe stirring. He glanced at Xiaoman's sleeve. "Brother Ma's mirror — you caught it." "He shone himself dry." "I won't touch you," said Qi Changsong. And he lowered his eyelids and said no more. The incense was lit.

Xiaoman walked once round him, and again. He went up and pushed, pushed his arm — like pushing a pillar; he hugged Qi Changsong round the waist and heaved, till his face went red, and Qi Changsong looked down at him like a man looking at a monkey hanging off a tree trunk. Xiaoman let go and backed to the edge, panting. The incense was half gone. Someone below yelled: "Layer two, come on down — don't keep the man from his supper!"

Xiaoman took the notebook from his coat and drew a sheet of yellow paper out of it. The crowd craned: a pig, with two pairs of wings on its back. "A charm?" "A charm drawn by a layer two?" "Is that a pig?" Xiaoman licked the back of the paper and slapped it on his forehead.

No wind. He stood at the edge with a pig stuck on his forehead, and waited. The laughter below rose in wave after wave; under the pagoda tree Money-Keeper Qian laughed his abacus right out of his hands. Xiaoman didn't laugh. His father had said: the moment the sun goes behind the hill, the mountain wind turns round — by day it climbs, by night it runs downhill; and the moment it turns, every deer in the wood lifts its head. Watch the wind first, then the deer.

The sun went down. The banner at the edge of the training ground first sagged, then flapped — whap — and turned over. The token on his chest warmed, very faintly, as if someone under a quilt had rolled over and let out one breath. Xiaoman's feet left the ground.

Up he floated, and not prettily: head first, backside after, legs pedalling in the air; first he hit the old cypress at the east corner — thunk — and bounced back; then the one at the west corner — thunk — and bounced back again. Below, people ducked and scattered with their arms over their heads; one inner-court senior had his topknot kicked crooked. He turned a circle in midair, and the pig on his forehead pointed at the centre of the stage and held still — at the centre stood a man, feet nailed into the stone, who hadn't moved a step in twenty years and stood more like a tree than any tree.

The pig-copter knew a tree when it saw one.

It dived, and Xiaoman went with it, head first, yelling "Waaah—!", straight at Qi Changsong's face.

Qi Changsong had stood for twenty years. But a boy with a pig on his forehead, howling, diving head-first at his face — in twenty years that had never happened. He frowned and stepped aside — just one step, very lightly, not a fold of his robe disturbed.

Xiaoman landed on the centre, face down, flat on the very point where the five slabs met, arms and legs spread like a New Year picture pasted on a door. The yellow paper on his forehead tore in two with a rip.

At that moment the steward struck the gong. The half stick was done.

The steward looked at the one lying on the centre, then at the one standing a step off it, opened his mouth twice, and said: "…Shen Xiaoman wins."

The training ground was silent a long while. Qi Changsong looked down at the foot he had moved, and looked a long time. "Twenty years," he said. Then: "That charm of yours — where did it come from?" Xiaoman picked himself up, holding his nose: "…Found it." Qi Changsong looked at him, said neither that he believed it nor that he didn't, gave him one nod, and walked down off the stage.

Champion: one Foundation pill. By temple custom the champion's name was to go into the blue register. Zhou Heng spread it open, turned back dozens of pages to the one with the stroke through it, looked, and turned forward again — in thirty years, the first time that line would hold an outer-court name. A stir at the back of the crowd: Ma Xiaobao was back, wrapped in his father's padded gown, ice in his hair, dripping all the way; he dripped up to the platform, saw the abbot placing a jade box in Shen Xiaoman's hands, stopped, opened his mouth, got nothing out, and shivered. In his hand he still clutched the cracked mirror — he hadn't let go of it even in the water. He looked at the cracked mirror, then at the fist Xiaoman held clenched at his side, and tucked the mirror inside his coat.

The jade box was bluish-white, a seal strip across its lid stamped with the abbot's great seal. Xiaoman put out his left hand to take it; his right was a fist, hidden in his sleeve. Xuanchenzi laid the box in his hand but didn't let go at once. He said mildly: "In the Chending hidden realm there is a stone chamber. For three hundred years, no one has gone in…" He didn't finish; he patted his shoulder, and walked away. Xiaoman stood holding the box, and the sweat broke out all down his back.

As he carried the box down off the platform he looked toward the gate. Elder Qu stood on the steps leaning on his broom, looking too. But he wasn't looking at Xiaoman; he was looking at the jade box in his hands. A long look, not like looking at a box, more like looking at something that happened many years ago. Then he turned away and swept.

At the foot of the steps Master Chu was waiting for him. Everyone had drifted off toward the kitchen; the old teacher stood there alone and held out two fingers: "Your wrist." Xiaoman offered his left. Chu didn't take it: "The other one." Xiaoman stood a moment, then brought his right hand out of his sleeve. Chu held it a long time, so long that over at the gate Elder Qu's broom began to sweep again. He turned the hand over, looked once at the palm, turned it back, and let go: "The pulse says layer two." He stroked his goatee, turned and walked away, and three steps on, without looking back, added: "The palm doesn't."
